# ggfourfold <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="200px" /><br><sub>Fourfold Displays for 'ggplot2'</sub>

***Package is a work in progress. Functionality may not work as intended.***

A `ggplot2` extension that provides a geom and theme for creating fourfold displays. Inspired by the `fourfold` SAS macro [@vcd:Friendly:2000] and `vcd` R package [@vcd:package].

## Installation

Install the latest version of `ggfourfold` from GitHub with:

```{r inst_ggfourfold, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gklorfine/ggfourfold")
```

## Overview

A fourfold display [@Friendly:94:TR217] is a visualization of a $2 \times 2$ table, or $2 \times 2 \times k$ tables via faceting. It consists of a circle that is split into quadrants, giving a segment for each cell in the table. In an **unstandardized** display, these quadrants have area proportional to the sample size of their corresponding cell. **Standardized** displays ... This helps with / affords / ... and gives a visual interpretation of the odds ratio, ...

## Examples

```{r libraries}
library(ggfourfold)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r ucb_unstd_noFacet}
ucb <- as.data.frame(UCBAdmissions)

ggplot(ucb, aes(x = Gender, y = Admit, weight = Freq)) +
  geom_fourfold(std = "ind.max") +  # For unstandardized display
  theme_fourfold()
```

```{r ucb_std_noFacet}
ucb <- as.data.frame(UCBAdmissions)

ggplot(ucb, aes(x = Gender, y = Admit, weight = Freq)) +
  geom_fourfold() +
  theme_fourfold()
```

```{r ucb_facet}
ggplot(ucb, aes(x = Gender, y = Admit, weight = Freq)) +
  geom_fourfold() +
  facet_wrap(vars(Dept), labeller = label_both) +
  theme_fourfold()
```

Quarter-squares can be drawn instead of quarter-circles with `shape = "square"`. Each square has the same area as the quarter-circle it replaces, so both shapes display a table with identical areas. Squares and their diagonal direction ticks can reach the corners of the frame where the cell counts are drawn; when they do in any panel, as here, the counts in every panel move just outside those corners.

```{r ucb_square}
ggplot(ucb, aes(x = Gender, y = Admit, weight = Freq)) +
  geom_fourfold(shape = "square") +
  facet_wrap(vars(Dept), labeller = label_both) +
  theme_fourfold()
```
